title: Activity holidays in the British Isles
titleCn: 英国群岛徒步活动假期咨询

paragraphs.text: Part one. You will hear a woman telephoning a holiday company to ask about activity holidays.
First, you have some time to look at questions one to four.
Now listen carefully and answer questions one to four.
Hello, Activity Holidays.
Oh, hello. I saw your ad about activity holidays in the British Isles. The one I was really interested in was in the Orkney Islands. They're in Scotland, aren't they?
That's right. So we run those holidays from June to September, and they're seven days. When were you thinking of going?
July.

Right. Let me check. We have two tours in July. Let's see. Yes, we still have places on the one beginning on July the 13th. Then we have another tour on July the 25th, but that's fully booked, I think. Yes.
I prefer the earlier date anyway. Okay, uh, well, can you tell me... It's a walking holiday, right?
Yes.
So what sort of level is it? I mean, I'm in pretty good shape, but...
Well, some of the terrain can be quite steep, so you do need to be reasonably fit. Overall, the tourist board has classified it as moderate.
Okay. Well, I should be able to manage that. And what about the accommodation?
Accommodation is in hotels. They're nothing too luxurious. They're mostly two-star hotels, but comfortable.
And I suppose breakfast is included?
Of course.
Okay, fine. And what about transportation?
Transport on the islands, you mean?
Yes.

Well, you'll be visiting four islands, so you'll be getting the ferry from one to another. And then on the islands, you'll use the bus when you're not walking. The train service is just on the mainland, so it's not much use to us.
Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions five to ten.
Now listen and answer questions five to ten.
And can you tell me some of the things we'll see?

Well, the scenery, of course, but there's a lot of history too. On the second day, you'll walk to Stenness Stone Circle. It's over five thousand years old. They think it was used to mark the passing of the seasons. And in fact, the site was known as the Temple of the Moon once upon a time.
Mm.
And the same day, you'll see some stones that date back to the same time, but they've got writing on them, which was done by invaders who came to the islands in the twelfth century.
I didn't realize the islands were invaded then.

Yes. Then on day three, you'll visit a village which dates back to the Stone Age, and that afternoon, you walk along the cliffs. You should have some good views. Then the next day, that's day four, you go on to Westray.
Oh, is that where there's a castle?

Yes. You spend a couple of hours there. And if you're interested in history, you'll also enjoy the walk on day five on Papay Island, where you'll have a chance to see a house that's actually supposed to be the oldest, not just in Scotland, but in the whole of Europe. It was buried for thousands of years and only recently uncovered by a storm. You'll stay on Papay for the Saturday night, and at the hotel, you'll be able to get a taste of the traditions of Scotland because they organize dancing there. All the locals take part as well as visitors. You'll certainly end up having a go yourself.
Well, it all sounds great. Now, what about the cost? It said six hundred and 55 pounds in the ad. So does that include the cost of getting to Scotland? I'm living in London.
No, that's just the holiday itself. Oh, and another thing, we do require you to take out insurance if you're not already covered. The one we recommend is Harvey Insurance Services.
Harvey?
Yes, that's H-A-R-V-E-Y.
Thanks. Well, I'd definitely like to go ahead with this. So what do I do now to reserve a place?

Well, we'll need to have a 10% deposit immediately, so you can pay that now by credit card, if that's okay. And then we'd ask you to send us the remaining amount 45 days before the start of the holiday.
Okay.
So could I have your card?
That is the end of part one. You now have one minute to check your answers to part one.
